newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore 3Q oil product output growth at 0.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: Singapore 3Q oil product output growth at 0.9 pct.

text.p: Singapore's petroleum product output for the third quarter of 1996 grew by a marginal 0.9-percent year on year, sharply lower than the 12 percent recorded in the previous quarter, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Friday.
"The petroleum products and petrochemicals industries were affected by both maintenance shutdowns and keen competition," the ministry said.
Petroleum product output grew seven percent in the first nine months of 1996 year-on-year, compared with a fall of 2.5 percent for the whole of last year.
Shell Singapore brought down a 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) crude distillation unit at its Bukom refinery for maintenance between July 8 and early September.

Singapore Refining Co (SRC) shut down a 60,000-bpd crude unit at its 285,000-bpd refinery for one week in early October. Low refining margins also forced Mobil Oil Singapore to cut refining runs at its 280,000-bpd refinery by 10 percent between mid-June and end-August.

Esso Singapore, an affiliate of US Exxon Corp reduced runs at its 230,000-bpd refinery by 15 percent between early July and end-October. Esso also shut a 110,000-bpd crude unit for three weeks in October.

Figures from the Monetary Authority of Singapore also showed there were no investment commitments in Singapore dollar terms in the petroleum sector in the third quarter, compared with S$65.2 million in the second quarter and S$43.1 million in the first quarter.
Investments in the petroleum sector in 1995 was S$1.19 billion, out of which S$593.2 million was invested in the third quarter.
